      Oct 26

      kevin peach

      USDA reports

      Traders have opinions as does everyone. Be careful on opinions. I am asked often my thoughts on reports but the one who has all the tools is USDA and is why they drive the market. We watch what demand does on rallies and price drops as that is a great opinion. As a producer you have to to look when cash needs are, profit levels are, when can you haul, carries etc and lock in prices. We do not sell when we know very bullish items but even then have a finger on avg sell button. Just a thought on USDA reports. We did see some nibbles on corn and beans on this price drop.If you are a Co-op customer and want our paid for Van Trump report call me or Chris. I really like his way of selling and reporting.

      With wheat adjusting to export values and crop weather for wheat areas of the north looking good it looks like new crop wheat gets binned and held off the market. Corn will also be as much as possible binned. Both waiting for a rally. We see beans at harvest going for cash and to free up bin space. Cash beans have held up and basis has narrowed. Advise is lock in basis on hedges. You will have extra cash beans to sell anyways. If behind on sales sell a few more. Tony Ho and Max Dobbler our corn and bean export team for UGC will be our speakers at this years annual meeting. July 16th at Turtle River State Park. I would NOT miss them as they are the ones who deal direct overseas and will be giving us a update on Asian sales.

      USDA takeaways

      What sticks out market wise. Wheat: lowest projected seeded acres since 1970. Managed money short wheat heading into spring which 7 out 10 times sees a rally.       I want to say hats off to everyone for the job of marketing a lower priced crop. Beans you sold last spring and balance this past few months. Building a price via carries and selling basis to match is best.       Feb 25

      kevin peach

      Basis vs cash vs building a price.

      I do talk a lot about basis and getting it right but getting futures and cash sold at a avg decent price is more important. Be careful not to get hung up on basis contracting only or who is paying a few penny's more. I have seen it to many times were great basis sales roll and turn into poor ones. Also futures move around way more than basis and getting them sold out the curve is so so important. IE selling new crop ahead and watching basis is good. Building a new crop cash that works. And there are times to sell basis but point is just to think basis is not best. Sometimes you miss the rally. It is also so so hard to hit the top so avg scale in is safest. Look at fundamentals but of course but listen to guys like Van Trump and his marketing. Its never about going for the fence. Its selling in a timeline for profit. Anyways lots of moving parts and marketing needs your time being spent daily on it. Any help you need please please call. Wade and myself for sure can walk through the markets. With the wind today we are closing at 3. in line by 2.30. Next week to help get grain off the farm to town we will be open 7.30-6 at Honeyford two pits for corn and one wheat.

We measure AM Thursday for year end so no dumping until 9 AM. Last day for wheat is Thursday at Honeyford as we have to stage for a corn shuttle mid next week. After corn train we will be back to wheat again. In line by 4.30. All basis levels steady at best.

      Feb 25

      kevin peach

      This week

      It was a very busy week. Futures run up brought out selling. Warm weather brought out haulers so pipelines are stocked. This is why on a non short crop year it works well to sell basis ahead when futures are lower and few are selling. Then on a futures rally you hit them. Or sell futures out the curve is really best and set basis on time periods were selling cash is light. Both work but generally selling cash on a futures run up you leave a little on the table. We liked selling 4.75 Dec corn futures and then rolling them out the curve later to build 5.00 plus futures price. Then hitting a -50 basis next winter for 4.50 cash. Wheat same strategy works. Its all about risk management and building a cash price. All basis levels this week are unchanged and we hit our target futures to trigger sales. Call to visit on markets.
